subject: Television & Streaming
title: Norman Lear and Social Television
description: A quick win: understand Norman Lear and Social Television.

hook.text: In 1971, Norman Lear put a loud racist on prime-time TV and made America laugh at him. The show was All in the Family.

buildup.text: Archie Bunker said things no TV character had ever said—about race, gender, and politics. Audiences were shocked.

discovery.text: Lear used comedy as a weapon. By making bigotry funny, he forced audiences to confront it instead of ignoring it.

twist.text: Some viewers loved Archie unironically. They saw him as a hero, not a satire. Lear never fully controlled the message.

climax.text: Lear created The Jeffersons, Maude, and Good Times—giving Black and feminist voices prime-time platforms for the first.

punchline.text: One producer forced America to laugh at its worst habits.

quiz.question: What was Norman Lear's strategy for addressing social issues on TV?
options: Using comedy to force audiences to confront bigotry
